headline: Meta Connect 2026 to feature new AI glasses, mixed reality headset, and more
summary: Meta's annual Connect event is scheduled for September 23, 2026, at 4PM PT/7PM ET. Expect major announcements across AI, smart glasses, and a new mixed reality headset.
details: Meta Connect 2026 is scheduled for September 23, starting with a keynote at 4PM PT/7PM ET. The event will cover Meta's hardware projects, AI advancements, and the metaverse.
New smart glasses are expected, reportedly including camera-free frames with enhanced microphones for Meta's AI assistant. This design aims to make them slimmer and address privacy concerns.
Other rumored glasses include a Gen 3 lineup of Meta Ray-Bans or an updated Meta Ray-Ban Display, potentially featuring displays in both lenses, sometimes referred to as "Hypernova 2."

A new mixed reality headset, codenamed "Phoenix," is also anticipated. Leaked images suggest a lightweight, goggle-like device that will rely on a tethered connection to a separate puck and support hand and eye tracking.

The Phoenix headset is expected to be among the first devices to use Qualcomm's new Snapdragon Reality Elite chip. This chip was specifically designed to support slimmed-down form factors for mixed reality devices.
Updates to HorizonOS are also likely, potentially promoting more entertainment-focused offerings. This could include a 3D horror series based on A24's 'Talk to Me,' designed for Meta's headsets.
Meta may also provide updates on its holographic avatars, first showcased two years ago with the Orion prototype. The technology is expected to eventually integrate into virtual reality experiences.
caption:
Meta Connect 2026 is set to unveil a new mixed reality headset, AI-powered smart glasses, and significant updates across its metaverse vision.

Meta Connect 2026 is scheduled for September 23, starting with a keynote at 4PM PT/7PM ET. The event will cover Meta's hardware projects, AI advancements, and the metaverse.

New smart glasses are expected, reportedly including camera-free frames with enhanced microphones for Meta's AI assistant. This design aims to make them slimmer and address privacy concerns.

Other rumored glasses include a Gen 3 lineup of Meta Ray-Bans or an updated Meta Ray-Ban Display, potentially featuring displays in both lenses, sometimes referred to as "Hypernova 2."

A new mixed reality headset, codenamed "Phoenix," is also anticipated. Leaked images suggest a lightweight, goggle-like device that will rely on a tethered connection to a separate puck and support hand and eye tracking.

The Phoenix headset is expected to be among the first devices to use Qualcomm's new Snapdragon Reality Elite chip. This chip was specifically designed to support slimmed-down form factors for mixed reality devices.

Updates to HorizonOS are also likely, potentially promoting more entertainment-focused offerings. This could include a 3D horror series based on A24's 'Talk to Me,' designed for Meta's headsets.

Meta may also provide updates on its holographic avatars, first showcased two years ago with the Orion prototype. The technology is expected to eventually integrate into virtual reality experiences.

headline: Meta's Muse AI agent overtakes ChatGPT as top free iPhone app, expands to Mac
summary: Meta's new Muse AI agent app has soared to the top of the free iPhone app charts in the U.S., surpassing ChatGPT, and is now also available on Mac for broader AI actions.
details: Meta's new Muse AI agent app has quickly climbed to the number one spot on the free iPhone app charts in the U.S. This achievement means it has surpassed OpenAI's ChatGPT in popularity on the iOS platform.

Beyond its success on iPhone, Muse has also launched on Mac, extending its capabilities to desktop users. The AI agent on Mac is designed to perform various actions directly on the computer, offering a more integrated experience.

Muse is an AI agent developed by Meta, aiming to provide users with advanced AI assistance for a range of tasks. Its rapid ascent in app store rankings highlights growing user interest in AI-powered tools for everyday use.
